issues.description: cad measure --holes without a part name errors with 'revision has 3 parts; name one' for multi-part assemblies; a default of all parts would be friendlier.
Docs do not say that rotating a Part by a Parameter in build() is the intended way to model pose, nor whether sweep checks pairs only (it reports only the closest pair, not every pair's minimum).
cad sweep prints only the single closest pair per pose, so the forearm-vs-arm gap (0.4 mm headroom) was not visible; I had to trust the min threshold.
cad measure --holes with several parts errors 'name one'; docs do not mention a part argument is required for multi-part projects.
cad sweep reports only the single closest pair per step, not every pair (arm<->forearm gap not shown).
cad measure --holes without a part name fails on multi-part assemblies ('name one'); inspect shows all parts but measure needs a part.
Shell heredoc file creation was blocked by the sandbox/permission layer; had to use the editor Write tool instead. Not a cad problem.
Docs do not state explicitly that Parameter() returns a plain number usable in arithmetic (it is implied by 'returns a plain number'); worked fine for center=(plate_width/2, ...).
cad measure with several parts requires a part name (error 'name one'); no all-parts option for --holes/--thickness.
Y sign conventions for XZ-plane slabs (offset=-y0, negative distance) and picking a 3D hole start point outside the part need care.

hole() with a 3D 'at' on a Y-axis hole whose start point lies outside the material (Y=0 vs a slab at Y -5.5..-0.5) fails with a generic BOOLEAN_FAILED 'hole cut failed' and no hint; the 2D form at=(x,z) works.
In this session, sed -i on files in the working dir required approval; unrelated to cad but slowed edits.
cad measure --holes without a part name errors on multi-part assemblies (must name a part); inspect/clearance work without one.
Rotation sign: rotate about y turns +Z toward +X, so a link hanging along -Z needs a negative angle to swing the foot toward +X. Easy to get backwards; verified via measure --holes at 90 deg.
cad sweep --render only rendered the requested view for the whole assembly under a long filename; render dirs are per revision (r2..r8), not named by angle.

Reference parts are returned from build() alongside the cradle; it was not obvious whether the task's 'one part named cradle' rule counts reference envelopes. Docs say they are skipped on export, which resolved it.

No direct check for 'keep-out region empty' (e.g. the volume above mid-plane or the 8 mm screw-head path); I verified by reasoning from the bbox and by modelling references. Modelling the keep-outs as reference parts would let cad clearance check them.
Shell heredoc writes to project files needed approval in the sandbox; had to use the file Write tool. Not a cad issue.

I did not model the sensor as a reference part, so cad clearance was not used; contact with the sensor (support) and the no-go regions were verified only by construction (cut with exact envelope cylinder, top at Z=25).
Unclear whether reference=True envelope parts count as extra parts for a 'one part named cradle' requirement; build output lists 4 parts.
Cylinder 'at' with axis='x' and align='min': it is not obvious that at gives the axis position (Y,Z) and the start X; I had to confirm from the clearance output.
cad clearance flags the intended bottom/top contacts as VIOLATIONs with --min, though per-face gaps show 'contact' for those faces only. Hard to tell allowed from forbidden contact at a glance.
cad clearance flags intended contacts (servo bottom/top, clamp on posts) as VIOLATION with --min 0.5; no way to whitelist allowed face contacts.
cad clearance flags intended bottom/top face contact (and bracket<->clamp seating contact) as VIOLATION with --min 0.5; no way to say 'contact allowed on these faces'.
Shell environment refused sed -i / braces in heredocs without approval; had to use Write for edits (environment, not cad).
`cad measure --holes` without a part name errors out on multi-part revisions ('name one') instead of listing all parts.
Not obvious from docs whether p.holes(..., direction='-z') with 2D `at` starts at the part's top face for a part located below Z=0; verified via measure --holes (it did).
No dedicated hex-nut pocket helper; had to extrude a regular_polygon cut at an offset plane (worked fine).

`cad measure --holes` without a part name errors on multi-part revisions ('name one'), while `cad inspect` works for all parts. Render with --section on multi-part revisions merges all parts into one file named clamp_top_clamp_bottom_*.
No direct check that two parts do not intersect (interference volume) or that the hex pocket flats are parallel to X; I relied on construction and a section render.

`cad clearance` errors with 'revision has 2 parts; name one' when no --part is given, although the docs say it checks every pair of parts. I could not get the pairwise touch/overlap check for the two halves, so 'must not intersect' was not verified numerically.
p.holes() is for holes entering from a face. I used extrude(Profile.circle, op='cut') at a Z offset to get the exact Z ranges for the through holes and the nut pockets.

suggestions.suggestion: cad sweep: print the min gap for every pair, not just the closest.
Let cad measure --holes/--thickness default to all parts.
Add an example for a multi-part moving assembly.
cad sweep should print min gap for every part pair
measure --holes without a part could loop over all parts
Let measure/query default to all parts
Report sweep per-pair min gap summary, not just the closest pair
Add a parametric-plate-with-hole_pattern example to the docs, showing center derived from a Parameter.
cad set leaves params.toml behind; a 'cad set --reset' / 'cad unset' command would be handy.
Add a one-line note in the docs that box(align=('min','min','min')) is the way to put a corner at the origin, next to the hole_pattern example.
Mention in the hole_pattern docs that center accepts expressions derived from Parameters, e.g. (w/2, h/2), as a typical use.
Let measure accept --all-parts.
Note in docs that positive rotation about Y swings a downward link toward -X (I had to negate knee_angle).
cad sweep could also produce one combined contact sheet.
Make BOOLEAN_FAILED for holes hint that a 3D start point not touching the material produces no cut; suggest the 2D at form.
Add an assembly example with a motion parameter on a rotated link layered along Y.
Let measure --holes/--thickness default to all parts.
Name sweep renders by parameter value (e.g. knee_angle_45_front.png).
A rotate_about helper with a 'point toward' hint or example for hanging links.
Add a keepout/envelope check helper that reports intersection with arbitrary boxes/cylinders.
Have cad clearance flag when a reference envelope touches a part, so it is clear whether contact is a support or an interference.
Provide a way to declare keep-out regions (e.g. cable cylinder, lift-out box) as reference parts with an example, and a check that a part touches a reference (distance 0) while not intersecting it.
Document that reference parts are excluded from deliverable part counts/exports.
Add a 'cad clearance' check that reports the contact area/points for 'must touch' requirements.
Offer a keep-out volume as a first-class reference check.
Let clearance mark specific faces of a reference part as allowed-contact, or print a per-face pass/fail against a min gap.
Allow 'cad measure --thickness' to report ligaments of holes in a named list.
Allow cad clearance to declare permitted contact faces or pairs.
A check for a vertical clear column above a point (e.g. screw-head or shaft path) would help.
Let cad clearance accept per-face allowed-contact rules (e.g. --allow-contact servo.bottom,servo.top) so the pass/fail exit code is meaningful for envelope tasks.
A built-in check for 'vertical column above a point is empty of all parts' (screw head / shaft keep-out) would help.
Let measure/inspect default to all parts when a revision has several.
Add a nut_pocket()/hex pocket feature with across-flats and orientation args.
Add an assembly-level interference check (cad clearance for non-reference parts) in docs for 'parts must not intersect'.
Add `cad interference` (or include in `cad clearance`) reporting overlap volume between non-reference parts.
Make measure --holes iterate over all parts by default.
Report hex pocket across-flats/orientation in find_holes-like output for polygon pockets.
Make `cad clearance` default to all pairs when a project has multiple parts.
Document a hex-pocket recipe (regular_polygon across_flats, angle=0 gives flats parallel to the u axis).
Let the 'cad measure --holes' output include hex pocket (non-circular) recesses.
